txt: He chuckles. "I am, at least in part, homes... until the Mother's love burns away the crude distinctions of the body."
He considers this for a moment. "I always thought of myself more like a *flame*. Flickering along the rafters and beams." He pauses. "It may be that I gotta work on my technique."
He laughs. "I don't mean *literal* singing, homes. This is the Mother of Silence we're talking about. It's the singing of a burning heart..."
He laughs. "Not sure I'm contributing to the economy none, homes."
He sighs. "It don't matter none, homes. Not anymore."
He sighs. "Things come back... in flashes. When something reminds me... Sometimes they even seem important again. *Really* important. But then, thanks to the Mother, they're gone again."
Is that... a man? Looks more like part of the carpentry of the building came alive and is now studying you intently.
Maybe it's possible to... talk to it?
The man leans forward a little, fixing you with a steady, unreadable gaze, then speaks...
The sinewy figure lingers on the wooden beams, blending into the shadows.
You see something hanging from the rafters, looking straight at you with dark eyes.
"*Estás crudo*, wey. I see deep inside you. Your body and spirit are suffering greatly from *overindulgment* and you don't even know it."
"*Un Cangrejo*!" He laughs. "Never thought of myself as a crab. More like... a flame flickering among the rafters and beams..." He pauses. "It may be that I gotta work on my technique."
"...now I use those same hands in service of something greater than my own restlessness."
"...the Mother will eat all of you, and never spit you out."
"...you may be thinking, 'But fire crackles!' No, homes, that's the material that's burning. The flames themselves are without sound."
"...your place among your fellows, your place in the world. I ain't got no use for such a place anymore."
"A boiadeiro? No, homes. I don't go in for that kinda thing. It's all about surrendering to the Mother now."
"Absolutely, man. Wouldn't bother me none to have 'em spin music in here. I'm usually way up there, imbibing."
"Been spending a lot of time here ever since. The past is nothing to me now, wey. It didn't belong to me."
"But I was talking about the singing of a burning heart... You may be thinking, 'But fire crackles!' No, homes, that's the material that's burning. The flames themselves are without sound."
"Chill out, man. Here you can receive the Mother's love, and, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
"Convenience has got nothing to do with what goes on up there..." He gazes up at the ceiling.
"Don't really follow her comings and goings. Just see her typing on her computer now and then. We've got different interests."
"Don't sweat it, vato. The password is 'AFTER LIFE DEATH.'"
"Don't think I've met one yet, homes." He studies you silently for a moment.
"Don't trust me -- trust the Mother. I'm only the messenger, homes." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
"Don't worry, man, you got a place -- right here." He sounds happy saying this, his limbs a mere shadow below the ceiling.
"Glad you're feeling more comfortable." He grins. "First-timers are always nervous."
"Good for you, man. But you must know that nothing you achieve's gonna make you happy and loved like you think you wanna be -- comes with being a slave to *el vino*."
"Habitual alcohol use has made you into a scared little pussy, homes. But don't worry, everything's gonna be alright -- you've come to the right place."
"Hard to say. I think I did some construction work here, back when I still had material worries. Up there, I realized what the true purpose of the church was..."
"Haven't you ever met a Mesque before, *cabron*? Surprising number of us around Revachol..."
"Here you can receive the Mother's love, and, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
"Hey, man. I see it in you -- you are prepared to surrender yourself to the fire of revelation. But you're still a bit shaky spiritually." He looks you over. "You're also just, physically, shaking."
"I ain't from no *marietti*, if that's what you're thinking. And the song I sing is silent as the Mother."
"I can see, and it saddens me. But devotion can save you -- it saved me."
"I can't leave my post here." He smiles. "Besides, it don't bother me none. Crab's no worse than a man, if you think about it."
"I circle it, nurtured by the silence bestowed by the Mother. One of these days, I'll be pure enough to go drink from it directly."
"I know it'll take time. Don't sweat it."
"I know it's hard to admit that you have a problem... I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look at the damage *el vino* was doing to my mind and my spirit."
"I know it's hard to admit that you've got a problem. I was like you once -- couldn't take an honest look into my own heart and see I was in pain."

"I think it was, a long time ago..." He looks at the red winter scarf in your hand. "I had to *shed* it like a skin, to get closer to the centre of the silence. You can have it. I don't need it anymore."

"I think they were, a long time ago..." He looks at the red brogues in your hand. "I had to *shed* them like skins, to get closer to the centre of the silence. You can have them. I don't need them anymore."

"I think they were, a long time ago..." He looks at the red clothing items in your hand. "I had to *shed* them like skins, to get closer to the centre of the silence. You can have them. I don't need them anymore."
"I think we're done here, ese." The figure crawls off into the darkness above.
"I told you, homes -- I don't know."
"I was in a gang, wey. But my memories of that time are fading... Most of them are already gone."
"I was like you once -- just dragging my feet to the next bottle... Shit was dark, homes."
"I will be incinerated, but not destroyed -- finally at one with the state of the world before reality began."
"I'm a saeraff, homes. I sing the Mother's glory."
"I'm afraid not, ese. You just have to wait until she comes back or..." He shrugs.
"I'm here to receive the Mother's love. You can, too, homes. And, when you're ready, she will take your hand and lift you out of the despair at the bottom of the bottle."
"I've done my share of illegal shit. Used to be in a gang, the whole deal. But even memories of that time are fading... Most of them are already gone."

"I've heard that before, wey." He shakes his head. "And I know I can't convince you on the spot. But think -- when's the last time you woke up from *silent communion* with a hangover, regretting what you did last night?"
"If you could submit to the mother -- sing her praises with your burning heart -- you could be free from selfish desire."
"If you was to surrender to the Mother -- you know, get a taste of *saeraffic* existence -- you'd never wanna go back."
"It don't bother me none. Crab's no worse than a man, if you think about it."
"It don't matter who *I* am, wey. I'm just bringin' you the message of the Mother's love. She don't want you to hang yourself on your own stubbornness." His words echo in the cold air of the church.
"It's all just for the Mother, man. No need to overthink it."
"It's not like that at all, man. It's just faith and joyful service."
"Keep the flame in your soul alive, though. One day you'll make it up here, if you put in the work."
"Look, man. I'm at liberty to talk about the sacred blaze of the Mother's glorious heart. But not about the coffee."
"Maybe I did." He sighs. "It don't matter no more."
"Might even be nice to have some company..."
"Naw, ese, it's not like that. Best thing that could happen to you -- losing your memory..."
"Naw, man. They look pretty funny. And I don't harm no one anymore anyway."
"Never known myself to be a *crab*. But if that's the name you've got for me, I won't stop you from using it."
"No worries, man. I know this shit takes time."
"No, I just call her 'viejita' because of her clothes, she's actually quite young..." He scratches his head. "Or maybe not *that* young... Age is just one of the many masks we wear."
"No, man, quite the opposite -- I don't think she cares much about authority or, anything else for that matter. Maybe only about her machines."
"No, man. You gotta let that shit go." He looks at you as if he wants to pat you on the back. "Then the Mother's light touch will fill you with rapture..."
"Not all of it. I was like you once. You don't know all the havoc *el vino* is wreaking on your mind and your spirit. Necesitas parar, homie."
"Not really, or at least I don't remember much of it anymore. The Mother's Love has done its job... That's what's so great about the Mother -- it lets you forget about everything."
"Oh hey, wey. There's coffee in the back... Oh, wait, I meant the Mother's love."
"Oh yeah, sure." His eyes remain fixed on yours. "You don't know anything about alcohol use. You've got it *all under control*, wey. I can smell the control all the way over here."
"Oh yeah, sure." His eyes remain fixed on yours. "You don't know anything about alcohol use. You've got it *all under control*, wey. I saw you hide that control behind your back."
"Oh, man, I'd love to see that statute." He pauses to think. "I'm sure I'd be 'trespassing' if the church was in use -- but it's not, hombre."
"Oh, that's no simple question, ese. She is one who can't be painted or sculpted..."
"Other spooker? Oh, esa viejita muy estudiosa!" He laughs. "Dunno, homes."
"Police raid a while back," he responds, his voice suddenly flat.
"Right on, homes. You're catching on. Yeah, you see, I'm sort of a saeraff to the Mother... I sing her glory."
"She is a cavity, in the dark, beyond sense. She saved me... but I couldn't describe her to you. No one can, homes, and no one ever will."
"She took you for a good spin, huh?" He looks at you gravely. "Don't worry, bro, that love is but a drop compared to the ocean of the Mother's love..."
"Something like that," he responds, his voice suddenly flat.
"Space? Jobs?" He laughs. "Do you see anyone taking swings at me for my place on the rafters?..."
"Sure am. Whittling wood used to be something I just did to busy my hands..."
"Sure did, homes."
"That's because you're soaked through and through with *al gul*, bro. Keeps you heavy and grounded. Then fools you into thinking that's a *good* thing."
"That's just the thing, homes -- none of that *matters*..." He ignores your hand, his limbs a mere shadow below the ceiling.
"That's just the thing, homes -- none of that *matters*..." He sounds melancholy saying this, his limbs a mere shadow below the ceiling.
"That's not quite right, but you're getting somewhere." He smiles enigmatically. "Any one of us could have been anything else..."
"That's not really the point, ese." He frowns. "You gotta give yourself over to service... Service of the Mother, that is..."
"That's what I said, homes."

"The grave's comin' for your little 'identity' sooner than you think, homes." He shakes his head sadly. "You sure you're ready? The Mother could set you free from all that shit." His words echo in the cold air of the church.
"The ones in the tent outside, right? I seen 'em. Guessing they're the ones who call me a crab? Probably scared of me..."
"The ones in the tent outside, right? I seen 'em. Think they're scared of me."
"The only thing we need to talk about is how the Mother can really help you, homes." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.

"Things come back... in flashes." He thinks for a moment. "When something reminds me... Sometimes they even seem important again. *Really* important. But then, thanks to the Mother, they're gone again."
"This is a special place. There's a perforation in the world up there. A way out, into nothingness." He nods toward the ceiling. "This church was built around it, for purposes of veneration."
"This is the Church of the Mother of Silence. You are welcome here." He sways gently on the beams, waiting for you to take it all in.
"Tiago is my name. But those syllables don't mean much to me these days. A name isn't just your identity, but also, so to speak..."
"Tiago's my name, by the way, though the syllables don't mean much to me. A name isn't just your identity, but also, so to speak..."
"Too many times, ese. You need it for something?"
"We are all one, who sing the Mother's glory."

"What were you even trying to do, man? I believe you can overcome your problems eventually, if you purge yourself of your wilfulness and seek the Mother's guidance. But *this*, right now, would be some suicidal shit."
"What you're suffering from is *el vino*-- it's left you alone with your selfishness. That's your tragedy, wey."
"What'd you think of that? Makes me almost pity *la nihilista pequeña* when I hear it."
"Why not? They wouldn't bother me none. I'm usually way up there, imbibing. Ain't no music on Earth that can reach where I go."
"Wouldn't bother me none to have 'em spin music in here. I'm usually way up there, imbibing."
"You just have to wait until she comes back or..." He shrugs.
"You know what this is. It's truth, homes. Join me, become one with it -- aflame with the Mother's love." His voice echoes in the cold air of the church.
"You know, I'm not so sure myself anymore." He thinks for a moment. "Don't really matter, though."
"You mean like a fugitive?" He glances at the abandoned radiocomputer on the other side of the nave, pulsing with light. Then he shakes his head.
"You've come back to face your cacodaemons. Good. You ain't gonna outrun them if you don't drop the bottle."
"You've really got a case of frayed nerves. *Pussy* in this usage comes from *pusillanimous*. Everybody knows that."
